15. /revoke is one atomic transition (KS-1278)

+

+ What this pins. POST /api/documents/:id/revoke decided + “already revoked” on a READ + (routes/documents.ts:2374) and then ran an unconditional + UPDATE. Two overlapping revokes could both pass that read, so both answered + 200, both wrote an action_provenance row and both emitted an + anchor call. The decision now lives IN the UPDATE: + updateDocument takes an ifStatusIsNot option that adds + AND (${guardStatus}::text IS NULL OR status IS DISTINCT FROM + ${guardStatus}::text) to the WHERE, and a guarded write that changed + no row returns null. The loser of the race answers the + same 400 BAD_REQUEST “Document is already revoked” as a + sequential caller, and returns before recordOnBehalfOf — so it + records no provenance row and emits no anchor. +

+

+ Scope. This completes the ticket’s scope — the atomic + transition, the 400 for the loser, and provenance and anchor only for the winner. The PR + says Refs KS-1278, not Closes. The row-lock alternative is + not taken. +

+

+ What a null from the guarded write means, and what each meaning is + pinned by. updateDocument already returned null for a + missing document (documentRepo.ts:543 at + 4a1620588819; :538 at the branch base 32e058975d4e), + so null is not a single condition and the route must not read it as one. On the + guarded path it can arise three ways: +

+
    +
  • A genuine race — another revoke changed the row between this + request's read and its write. The write refuses in the UPDATE, so exactly one of two + overlapping writers wins. Instrument: cell R1, which also asserts + 0 anchor emissions on the losing path, not only 0 provenance rows. The + guard itself is pinned by cell R2, which asserts the guard clause by + exact text and the guard’s own two parameters by + position — a weaker assertion on either half is satisfied by a vacuous + guard, or by the SET clause’s new status standing in for the guard + value.
    • +
  • The row was deleted inside the window — the answer is 400 where + 404 belongs. This is unchanged by round 2 and is tracked as + KS 1419. Instrument: none live — unmeasured + against a real database.
    • +
  • A revoke addressed by the platform UUID — fixed in round 2. + Both reads fall back to the primary key for a UUID-shaped id + (documentRepo.ts:244-251) and the API hands clients that key as + documentUuid (:172), but the guarded UPDATE keyed on + external_id. At the branch base and at round 1 a sequential, + non-race revoke of a live, owned, unrevoked document addressed that way matched 0 rows and + answered 400 "Document is already revoked" with 0 provenance rows and the + status never written. At round 2 the guarded write keys on the row the read + resolved (:616, mirroring the read's own precedence: external_id + first, then the primary key), so it answers 200, writes the status and records + exactly one provenance row. Instrument: cell N1, red at + 4a1620588819 and green at the round-2 head.
    • +
+

+ The route still 404s at :2367 and 403s at :2371 before the write, so + a missing or unowned document never reaches it. Only the opted-in revoke path changed + key: the other 12 production updateDocument( callers pass no + ifStatusIsNot and take a byte-identical statement + (instrument: cell N3). A non-UUID external id never reaches the + ::uuid cast, which would otherwise raise 22P02 (:590; + instrument: cell N2, green at both ends).
